title: Benchmark catalog, comparison UI, and anomaly triage playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a searchable, versioned benchmark catalog and a lightweight comparison UI that surfaces regressions and makes triage fast. This ticket covers the end-to-end triage playbook: storage schema, comparison UX, automated anomaly flags, and human workflow for investigating p95/throughput regressions (tokens/sec).
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff - aligned on scope with PM and Design. Decided to store benchmark runs as immutable artifacts and attach runtime metadata (kernel config, quantization, batch size).

2025-02-18: Spike complete - PoC for compact result payloads (summary + compressed per-step samples). Storage estimate: ~70KB per run for full traces, 4KB for summaries. Chose compressed NDJSON blobs for trace retention.
2025-02-24: Design feedback - UX should default to token/sec and p95 delta, with an option to view full time-series. Design suggested side-by-side delta columns and a small sparkline per metric.

2025-02-27: Engineering decision - use a two-tier storage model: hot TSV-like summaries in Postgres (one row per run, fast filters) + cold compressed traces in S3 with lifecycle rules. This balances query speed vs cost.
2025-03-03: PR opened for API & DB migrations: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-api/pull/2314. First integration test passes in CI but flaky on long-run ingestion; working on backpressure tuning.

2025-03-04: Implemented basic anomaly rules: (1) p95 increase > 15% vs baseline AND absolute p95 > target, (2) tokens/sec drop > 20% vs baseline. Alerts flow to #bench-triage with a link to comparison UI.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog storage: run summary schema stored and queryable by model, commit, sequence_length_bucket, batch_size, quantization_profile, and runtime_version
Comparison UI: show two runs side-by-side, highlight metric deltas (p50,p95,tokens/sec), and render sparkline of per-step latency
Anomaly detection: automated rule engine flags regressions and creates a triage card with links to traces and a suggested baseline run
Triage playbook: documented steps to reproduce locally, checklist for kernel/kv-cache/quantization diffs, and escalation path to runtime core
End-to-end test: ingest synthetic benchmark bundle, trigger anomaly rule, and verify triage card can reproduce the run from S3 traces
notes:
Implementation notes:
- Summary row fields: run_id, model, model_version, commit_hash, hardware_type, runtime_version, sequence_len_bucket, batch_size, quant_profile, tokens_total, tokens_per_sec_mean, tokens_per_sec_p50, tokens_per_sec_p95, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, sample_count, created_at, trace_s3_key.
- Trace format: compressed NDJSON of per-token step durations (for debugging pathological cases).
- Retention: summaries retained indefinitely; traces TTL 90d by default, configurable per-customer.
- Query patterns prioritized: filter by model+version, group by runtime_version, top-n regressions by delta p95.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Chose Postgres for summaries to leverage ad-hoc queries and joins to PR metadata. Could have used timeseries DB but cost + complexity higher for small cardinality.
- Compressed traces in S3 to keep storage costs predictable; adds small latency when loading full trace in UI but acceptable for triage flows.
- Thresholds are intentionally conservative (15% p95 / 20% tokens/sec) to reduce noisy alerts; we will tune with live data in first two weeks.

Triage playbook (short):
1) On alert, open comparison UI -> the system will suggest a baseline run (most recent green run on same commit window).
2) Check delta columns: p95 and tokens/sec first. If p95 regressed but tokens/sec stable => investigate kernel/latency regressions (scheduling/kv cache).
3) If tokens/sec dropped significantly -> investigate batching, sequence length distribution, and host-level saturation (CPU/GPU util).
4) Re-run synthetic harness locally with identical runtime_version and quant_profile using bench-ingest replay tool. Attach run_id to triage card.
5) If reproduction fails, add 'needs infra' label and escalate to infra oncall with collected metrics (perf counters, dmesg, traces).

Notes on instrumentation and alerts:
- Provide per-run histograms of latency; use P-square algorithm in the ingest pipeline to preserve p95 cheaply.
- Alert payload includes baseline run_id, delta percentages, top-3 abnormal traces (S3 keys), and a one-click repro link that launches a cloud job to reproduce the run.

Open questions:
- Do we want per-customer retention policy override in the UI? PM leaning yes for enterprise customers.
- Should anomaly rules be configurable per-project or global? Start global, add project-level overrides in a follow-up.
